title: The phases of the Moon, in order
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: The Moon does not change shape. Half of it is always lit by the Sun, and as it circles Earth we see more or less of that lit half. Learn the eight names and you can tell, just by looking, whether the Moon is growing or shrinking and when it will be full.

How to hold it: Start from the idea, not the words: a ball lit from one side, seen from different angles. Try it with a lamp and an orange. Then learn two word pairs: waxing means growing, waning means shrinking; crescent is less than half, gibbous is more than half. The eight names now build themselves in two chunks of four. In the Northern Hemisphere, D-O-C helps: a growing Moon is lit on the right like a D, full is an O, and a shrinking Moon is lit on the left like a C.
